card.alive_premise: Everyone else knows the finished version. One partner knows the terrible first version so well they can still perform it from memory.
card.moment_origin_detail: Generic relationship hypothesis about one partner repeatedly witnessing the other rehearse an evolving speech, pitch, routine, story, or creative work; no Aachu/Zuv rehearsal history is claimed.
card.title: They Knew the Bad Version by Heart
card.concrete_moment: During a polished presentation, one partner in the audience mouths an awkward beat that was removed many drafts ago. Past rehearsals reveal why: the witness heard every false start until the deleted version became shared memory.
card.universal_truth: The deepest witness is often not the person who applauds the polished result, but the person who knows the rough version by heart because they were present while it changed.
card.audience_mirror: Couples where one person has endured repeated practice runs, unfinished stories, awkward presentations, exam answers, jokes, speeches, or other work-in-progress versions.
card.scroll_stop: At the polished presentation, the audience partner performs an obviously wrong old beat at exactly the same time as the person on stage.
card.emotional_contradiction: Knowing the obsolete bad version seems like ammunition for teasing, but reveals an intimacy unavailable to the audience applauding the finished work.
scene_proof: The witness anticipates a removed line or gesture during the current polished version.
An earlier rehearsal shows a false start and the witness resetting a timer or taking the familiar practice position.
Successive rehearsals change location, pages, and delivery while the obsolete fragment recurs.
After the public moment, the couple privately reenacts the discarded version together.
card.relationship_motion: The maker moves from cringing at the obsolete version to joining the reenactment; the witness moves from rehearsal audience to keeper of a private history.
retention_ladder: Why does the audience partner know a line absent from the finished version?
The first rehearsal reveals it began as a mistake.
Repeated attempts show the witness absorbing the work through proximity.
The polished version removes every trace of the awkward beginning.
The couple deliberately reenacts the bad version together after the applause.
card.payoff: Public love can applaud the final version; private love sometimes knows the deleted version by heart.
card.dm_send_reason: It is naturally sendable to the partner who heard every practice run and remembers the embarrassing version nobody else knows existed.
card.format_recommendation: Illustrated carousel with a wrong-beat cold open, rehearsal escalation, polished public contrast, and private reenactment.
card.asot_turn: Use affectionate embarrassment and mutual reenactment instead of solemn encouragement; comic muscle memory becomes proof of years spent close to the making.
card.novelty_fingerprint: obsolete rehearsal beat resurfaces at polished event + witness knows deleted version + comic error becomes intimate history
risks: A generic supportive-partner montage would weaken the route.
The incident needs a creator-confirmed form of repeated practice before personalization.
The witness must not be framed as tolerating a burdensome partner.
